# One Chain

<!-- STEP id="clash" -->
Our wants have no end, but resources such as money, time, land and steel are limited. When unlimited wants meet limited resources, we face **scarcity**.

<!-- STEP id="choice" -->
Scarcity forces us to choose. Meera chooses how to spend her money, the farmer chooses a crop, and the government chooses what to build. Every choice has an opportunity cost: the next-best thing we give up.

<!-- STEP id="three" -->
For a whole economy, these choices become three key questions: what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce. Economic systems answer them in different ways, and most economies today mix the market and the government.

**Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost are the building blocks of economics.**
